newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says no foreign pressure to abolish band.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says no foreign pressure to abolish band.

text.p: Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Thursday the government's decision to abolish the rupiah intervention band was not taken because of pressure from foreign governments or institutions.

"I want to stress here that this country is a sovereign country and we are fully (in charge) of deciding what is the best according to our perspective, according to the situation," Mar'ie told a news conference.

Mar'ie said the government move was perceived by the international community as a good decision and this decision showed the country was quick to give the right response at the right time to currency fluctuations.
Meanwhile, central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono told the conference that the move was realistic and that it was not a surprise decision.
"We want to be realistic in seeing the situation. Seeing the current situation, this appears to be the best decision," he said.
"Of course these days people want to know precisely why, they want to take positions. We are really committed every time we apply a system. Don't see this as a surprise thing," Sudradjad said.
